commits.pr_title: [Misc] Use VLLMValidationError in offline inference input validation
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Part of #48227 Step 5.

Migrate the three caller-caused length-mismatch errors in `OfflineInferenceMixin`
(`vllm/entrypoints/offline_utils.py`) from raw `ValueError` to `VLLMValidationError`:

- `_params_to_seq` — prompt/params count mismatch
- `_lora_request_to_seq` — prompt/lora_request count mismatch
- `_priority_to_seq` — prompt/priority count mismatch

This file is the generate-side counterpart of `vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/io_processor.py`,
migrated in #51931 — `OfflineInferenceMixin` and `PoolingIOProcessor` each carry their own
copies of these three helpers with identical messages. The pooling side was migrated; the
generate side still raised raw `ValueError`, so the same failure surfaced as a different
exception type depending on which entrypoint the caller used:

```
generate side _params_to_seq  -> ValueError
pooling  side _params_to_seq  -> VLLMValidationError
                                 (identical message in both cases)
```

All three are reachable from the public offline API: they are called from
`_add_completion_requests` and `_add_chat_requests`, `OfflineInferenceMixin` is a base of
`LLM`, and `params`, `lora_request` and `priority` are public parameters of
`LLM.generate()`, `LLM.enqueue()` and `LLM.enqueue_chat()`, documented as having to match
the length of `prompts`.

Existing messages and validation behavior are unchanged. These paths are offline-only
(`LLM`, not `AsyncLLM`), so there is no HTTP status-code change; the benefit is that
offline callers can catch a semantic type instead of a bare `ValueError`.

### Difference from #51931

That PR deliberately left `_priority_to_seq` as a raw `ValueError` because it was not
reachable through the public pooling paths. On the generate side it *is* reachable, via
`LLM.generate(..., priority=[...])`, so it is migrated here. Happy to drop it if you would
rather keep the two sides symmetric.

### Updated existing assertions

`VLLMValidationError` no longer inherits from `ValueError`, so four existing assertions that
expected `ValueError` from these paths are updated to expect the semantic type:

- `tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py` — params mismatch, priority mismatch, empty priority list
- `tests/lora/test_qwen3_with_multi_loras.py` — lora_request mismatch

`BeamSearchOfflineMixin` also inherits `_params_to_seq` and `_lora_request_to_seq`, so beam
search callers see the same type change. No existing test asserts `ValueError` on those paths.
`PoolingOfflineMixin` is unaffected: it goes through `PoolingIOProcessor`'s own copies.

`parameter`/`value` are left unset, consistent with #51753 and #51931 — these helpers serve
`generate`, `chat` and `enqueue`, whose public argument names differ (`params` is exposed as
`sampling_params` on `generate()`).

## Duplicate-work check

I searched open PRs for #48227, `offline_utils`, `OfflineInferenceMixin`, `_params_to_seq`
and `_priority_to_seq`, and inspected the current `main` implementation. I found no open PR
migrating these errors. #48544 touches the same file for an unrelated tokenization speedup
and is a stale draft; it mocks these helpers in tests but does not modify the raise sites.

AI assistance disclosure: Claude Code assisted with the audit, implementation, test
generation and review. I reviewed and understand all changed lines and validated the
behavior locally.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/test_offline_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py \
    tests/lora/test_qwen3_with_multi_loras.py --collect-only -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/offline_utils.py \
    tests/entrypoints/test_offline_utils.py \
    tests/entrypoints/llm/test_generate.py \
    tests/lora/test_qwen3_with_multi_loras.py
```

## Test Result

```text
4 passed in 0.37s
9 tests collected
All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
```

I also verified the new tests fail against unmodified `main` (3 failed, 1 passed), confirming
they exercise the change rather than passing vacuously.

The model-backed suites (`test_generate.py`, `test_qwen3_with_multi_loras.py`) were not
executed locally — they require a real model and this was developed on an Apple Silicon CPU
build. They are verified to collect, and their updated assertions are covered by CI.

Environment note: `requirements/test/cpu.txt` is compiled for `x86_64-manylinux` and does not
install on arm64 macOS, so only `tblib` was installed to satisfy `tests/conftest.py`.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Pin Cython below 3.3 for arm64 tilelang sdist
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the deterministic arm64 image-build failure caused by Cython 3.3 while building `tilelang==0.1.12` from source. No test runs: the image fails during dependency installation.

Exact reproductions on the restored immutable builder image:

- [PR-head arm64 image #85174](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85174#01a02917-5821-464a-a258-251e2db3a874)
- [post-merge main arm64 image #85175](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85175#01a02919-9021-4add-9b37-90cc0c58feb6)

## Root cause

The aarch64 build base is manylinux 2_28 / glibc 2.28, so it cannot install tilelang's `manylinux_2_34` aarch64 wheel and uv builds tilelang from sdist. Fresh isolated builds now resolve Cython 3.3, which rejects tilelang's hardcoded `Py_LIMITED_API=0x03080000` because Cython 3.3 requires Python Limited API 3.9 or newer. The previous successful build used the same immutable builder before Cython 3.3 was released, so it resolved an older compatible Cython.

## Change

On aarch64 only, set uv's isolated-build constraint to `cython<3.3` before installing CUDA requirements. x86_64 continues to install tilelang's wheel and is unaffected. CMake is no longer constrained; the restored builder remains on its existing CMake 4.4.2.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `cython arm64 tilelang`, `cython 3.3`, and `tilelang build`. This PR was already the only open match, so it was narrowed in place instead of opening a duplicate.

## Test status

- `uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files docker/Dockerfile`: passed, including Dockerfile dependency-graph and `versions.json` validation.
- Exact updated-head [arm64 image #85232](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85232#01a02d89-31bf-4713-b188-ac28da85fb9f) at `66ad0efdceb4`: passed exit 0 in 39m34s, including the tilelang sdist build and complete vLLM image build/push under CMake 4.4.2.
- Merged as main `e25c586b9030`; [post-merge main arm64 #85235](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85235#01a02dac-36a1-413f-a4a1-dffd0b5d1e56) passed exit 0 in 39m21s, including the complete image build and registry push.
- [Post-merge GH200 #85236](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85236#01a02db0-c858-4867-8ff8-39e6a55d443d) at `7f17348fd67c` (exact merge commit plus only the selector scaffold `key: gh200-test` on a non-main validation branch) completed the full wheel build and reached Docker `build 17/17` with neither build-tool failure. It stopped only at the separately baseline-known wheel-size gate: 561.96 MB > 500 MB (baseline #84342: 552.17 MB > 500 MB). No retry.

Post-merge arm64 and GH200 both cleared the Cython/Limited-API and fatal CUDA imported-location signatures. This incident is resolved on main; the GH200 wheel-size gate remains separate baseline debt.

## AI-assistance disclosure

This change was prepared with AI assistance and reviewed before submission.

## Purpose

Follow up to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53275

As summarized by Qwen-3.8 Max:

### Core change

`PromptSeq = str | list[int]` → `list[int]` everywhere.

The biggest win is not the alias swap — the matcher loses the tokenizer
entirely:

| Signature now | After |
|---|---|
| `iter_token_matches(prompt, tokenizer)` | `iter_token_matches(prompt)` |
| `_plan_prompt_updates(prompt, updates, tokenizer)` | `_plan_prompt_updates(prompt, updates)` |
| `apply_token_matches(prompt, updates, tokenizer)` | `apply_token_matches(prompt, updates)` |
| `find_mm_placeholders(prompt, updates, tokenizer)` | `find_mm_placeholders(prompt, updates)` |
| `is_embed(tokenizer, full)` | `is_embed(full)` |
| `_GetMatchIndex(tokenizer, prompt, start_idx)` | `_GetMatchIndex(prompt, start_idx)` |

`vllm/renderers/hf.py` already passes `tokenizer=None` — proof that the
engine only needs it for `str` conversion.

### What gets deleted

- `PromptSeq`, the `_S` TypeVar, `PromptUpdateDetails(Generic[_S])`
  → plain `full: list[int]`
- `_seq2text`, `_seq2tokens`, `_cached_encode`, `_cached_decode` (as shared API)
- `iter_text_matches`, `apply_text_matches`,
  `apply_text_matches_as_segmented_tokens`, `_apply_text_matches*` methods
- The `str` branch in `_target_key`, dual normalization in
  `PromptIndexTargets.prefix`
- The `regex` import — `re.finditer(re.escape(x))` is just a substring scan;
  a `str.find` loop replaces it
- The `cast(list[_S], out_seqs)` hack in `_apply_matches`
- The whole "cannot encode/decode with `skip_tokenizer_init=True`" error class

### What must survive (privatize, don't delete)

The BPE fallback in `_apply_prompt_updates` (~line 1688): a
non-special-token target can tokenize differently inside the prompt
(`"foo"` inside `"food"`). Token-ID targets do not fix this —
`encode("foo")` still won't match a merged `"food"` token. So keep:
decode prompt → substring match → re-encode. But:

- Make it a private helper, driven by `list[int]` targets (decode the target
  internally).
- `BaseMultiModalProcessor` owns it via `self.info.get_tokenizer()`; the pure
  engine stays tokenizer-free.
- The `minicpmv` override keeps its segmented variant
  (`_apply_text_matches_as_segmented_tokens`): it encodes segments separately
  to avoid BPE merges across segment boundaries (see the comment around
  `apply_text_matches_as_segmented_tokens`).

## Test Plan

- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Mistral3: fix image placeholder grid for processor size overrides
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`Mistral3MultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates` currently computes the image placeholder grid via `PixtralHFEncoderInfo.get_patch_grid_size`, which uses `vision_config.image_size` as the max edge. It ignores `mm_processor_kwargs={"size": {"longest_edge": N}}` and any `preprocessor_config.json` whose `size.longest_edge` differs from `vision_config.image_size`, so the placeholder count no longer matches the `pixel_values` geometry emitted by the HF `PixtralProcessor` and inference fails with:
```
RuntimeError: Expected there to be N prompt placeholders corresponding to
N image items, but instead found M prompt placeholders! ...
```
This PR derives `ncols`/`nrows` directly from `out_mm_kwargs["image"][item_idx]["pixel_values"].data.shape[-2:]` divided by `patch_size * spatial_merge_size` — the effective post-`Mistral3PatchMerger` grid stride. HF's `PixtralImageProcessor.get_resize_output_image_size` rounds resized dims to a multiple of that stride, so the floor divides are exact.
No checkpoint, output-shape, or user-facing API changes.

## Test Plan

```
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/mistral3.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py
pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py
```

## Test Result
- Pre-commit hooks, Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and repository checks: passed.
- `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_mistral3.py`: all cells passed across `mm_processor_kwargs ∈ {{}, {"size":{"longest_edge":1008}}, {"size":{"longest_edge":1288}}}`, image sizes `{(1540,1540), (1536,1187), (2200,1700)}`, `num_imgs ∈ {1, 2}`, and both `kwargs_on_init` modes.
- Standalone reproduction on `mistralai/Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct-2503`: before the patch, requests with a `longest_edge` override raise the "N prompt placeholders … found M" runtime error; after the patch, every case succeeds and the placeholder count matches the raw HF processor's `pixel_values` geometry.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

- Honor the existing `CONTAINER_TIMEOUT_S` budget for single-node Docker AMD jobs.
- Subtract runner setup time before starting the workload timeout so the reserved teardown minute is not consumed by image/setup work.
- Keep interactive Docker execution in the foreground, send `TERM` at the deadline, and escalate to `KILL` after 10 seconds if needed.
- Preserve normal Docker workload exit statuses, report deadline expiry as status 124, and emit focused timeout lifecycle logs.

The AMD CI template already computes `CONTAINER_TIMEOUT_S` one minute before the Buildkite step timeout and exports it to the runner, but the runner did not consume it. A single-node Docker workload could therefore reach the hard step timeout before the runner regained control for its existing exact-name container cleanup and diagnostics.

This change makes that existing budget effective. It bounds only `docker run` and then relies on the runner's existing `EXIT` cleanup path.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Restore attention coverage after KV-cache layout refactor
commits.pr_body:
This is a follow-up to #51718, which standardized KV-cache layouts but also changed several ROCm test paths. It realigns FlexAttention tests with production and restores coverage for relevant AITER safety and MLA paths. It also avoids generating CUDA-only MLA prefill parameter matrices on ROCm, reducing collection from 2,911 to 591 cases. Together, these changes improve regression coverage while modestly reducing test resource usage.

- Build MLA prefill backend parameters positively by platform, using the CUDA backends on CUDA and `ROCM_AITER_FA` on ROCm.
- Exercise the production ROCm MLA combination by adding `ROCM_AITER_MLA` to the main backend matrix while retaining `ROCM_AITER_FA` for prefill.
- Restore FlexAttention direct-mask coverage on ROCm and retain slow-path coverage for sliding-window and non-causal attention without duplicating encoder-only execution.
- Restore the MiniMax M3 AITER multi-KV-head guard test and validate the follow-up on AITER-enabled MI355X GPUs.

## Purpose

`--attention-config.use_prefill_decode_attention` is accepted, documented, and
has no effect.

It used to select `ROCM_ATTN` on ROCm. #36702 made `ROCM_ATTN` the
unconditional first entry in the ROCm priority list and removed the branch that
read the flag, so the field has had no reader in `vllm/` since. Its original
purpose is now the default behaviour, making this leftover surface rather than
a regression.

Two tests suggest otherwise: `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py` asserts the flag
parses, and the `RocmAttn` entry in `tests/v1/attention/utils.py` passes it
beside an explicit `"backend": "ROCM_ATTN"`.

## Modifications

This opened as stage 1 of the
[deprecation pipeline](docs/contributing/deprecation_policy.md) — a warning
naming v0.29.0 for removal. Per review, the flag is now removed outright:

- delete `use_prefill_decode_attention` from `AttentionConfig`
- drop it from the `RocmAttn` test config; the explicit backend selection is
  unchanged, so behaviour is identical
- drop the parse assertions from `test_attention_config`

The pipeline exists to give users notice before behaviour changes under them.
Here there is no behaviour to preserve: the flag's effect is already the
unconditional default, so no working configuration changes meaning. The only
user-visible difference is that passing the flag now raises instead of being
silently ignored, which surfaces a setting that was already doing nothing.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py
```

## Test Result

`97 passed`. `pre-commit` passes on the three changed files, mypy included.

`grep -rn use_prefill_decode_attention` over the tree returns nothing after
this change.

## Notes

Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue references `use_prefill_decode_attention`.

No evals included; the flag has no consumer and there is no runtime change.

AI assistance was used for this change. I have reviewed every changed line and
run the tests above.

cc @gshtras (authored #36702), @yewentao256 (reviewed)

## Purpose

Add framework support for using a `Qwen3OmniDSparkModel` draft architecture with a Qwen3-Omni thinker target.

This change:
- registers the dedicated Qwen3-Omni DSpark architecture while reusing the shared `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` runtime implementation;
- exposes the target thinker's post-DeepStack auxiliary hidden states required by DSpark;
- preserves the dedicated architecture and DSpark sampling fields when converting msModelSpec configuration;
- validates the target/draft hidden size, attention geometry, target-layer selection, vocabulary contract, and DSpark algorithm settings at startup;
- makes embedding and lm-head sharing safe when the draft input/output vocabulary differs from the target vocabulary;
- relies on the draft-logits cache stride fix from #53017 instead of maintaining a model-specific resizing workaround;
- adds focused registry, configuration, model-contract, and configuration-bridge tests.

A repository search for `Qwen3 Omni DSpark` and `Qwen3OmniDSpark` found no existing PR implementing this support, so this does not duplicate known work.

This is a framework integration PR. Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoints are not yet available, so it does not claim model quality or acceptance-rate results.

AI assistance disclosure: this PR was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. The submitter is responsible for reviewing every changed line and completing the required NPU/model evaluation.

commits.pr_title: [Pooling] Fix Rust pooling endpoint for benchmark
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Rust `vllm-pooling` benchmark defaulted to `/v1/pooling`, while vLLM only serves `/pooling`, causing documented commands to return 404. This PR updates the client default and documentation with the server route.

## Main vs branch validation

Tested revisions:

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import re
import subprocess

from vllm.entrypoints.pooling.pooling.api_router import router


def endpoint_at(ref: str) -> str:
    source = subprocess.check_output(
        ["git", "show", f"{ref}:rust/src/bench/src/cli.rs"],
        text=True,
    )
    match = re.search(
        r'BackendKind::VllmPooling\s*=>\s*"([^"]+)"\.to_string\(\)',
        source,
    )
    assert match is not None
    return match.group(1)


server_routes = {route.path for route in router.routes}
results = {
    "upstream/main": endpoint_at("upstream/main"),
    "fix-rust-pooling-endpoint": endpoint_at("HEAD"),
}

print(f"server_routes={sorted(server_routes)}")
for ref, endpoint in results.items():
    status = "PASS" if endpoint in server_routes else "FAIL"
    print(
        f"{ref}: default_endpoint={endpoint}, "
        f"route_exists={endpoint in server_routes}, status={status}"
    )

assert results["upstream/main"] not in server_routes
assert results["fix-rust-pooling-endpoint"] in server_routes
print("Main reproduces the endpoint mismatch; branch resolves it.")
PY
```

### Results

```text
server_routes=['/pooling']
upstream/main: default_endpoint=/v1/pooling, route_exists=False, status=FAIL
fix-rust-pooling-endpoint: default_endpoint=/pooling, route_exists=True, status=PASS
Main reproduces the endpoint mismatch; branch resolves it.
```

| Revision | Rust default | Server route exists | Result |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `upstream/main` | `/v1/pooling` | No | Reproduces bug |
| Branch | `/pooling` | Yes | Passed |


## Regression Tests



commits.pr_title: [Core][RL] Support sparse checkpoint updates through native weight loaders
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose ### Motivation Online RL trainers commonly produce updates in checkpoint/Hugging Face coordinates: a checkpoint name, the full checkpoint shape, and either a dense tensor or flat changed indices and values. These coordinates are not the same as vLLM's runtime parameter coordinates. For example, a checkpoint tensor may be split across tensor-parallel ranks, packed with another checkpoint tensor, or mapped into expert-parallel runtime weights. The existing `sparse_nccl` backend expects an already-resolved runtime parameter name and rank-local indices, so it cannot serve as a general bridge for checkpoint-coordinate updates. This PR adds a small model-loader API that keeps the model's native `model.load_weights()` path as that bridge. The native loader continues to own checkpoint-name mapping, TP/EP placement, and packed/model-specific layouts. ### Design ```mermaid flowchart LR A["One patch-loading call
checkpoint name, full shape/dtype,
values and optional flat indices"] A --> B{"All patches in this call"} B -- "Dense" --> C["Build full checkpoint tensors"] B -- "Sparse" --> D["Build full checkpoint-shaped NaN tensors
index_copy_ fills changed checkpoint positions"] C --> L["One or more model.load_weights(...) calls
native checkpoint-to-runtime mapping
for TP/EP and packed/model-specific layouts"] D --> P["Temporarily replace process-wide
torch.Tensor.copy_
during each serialized sparse loader call"] P --> L L -- "Dense: native loader semantics" --> U["Runtime tensors updated"] L -- "Sparse: each Python Tensor.copy_" --> E{"Floating source and destination
with the same shape?"} E -- "Yes" --> M["Cast source, merge with
where(isnan(source), destination, source),
then call the original copy_"] E -- "No" --> N["Call the original copy_ unchanged
unsupported for sparse patches"] L -. "Sparse custom or non-copy_ write" .-> X["Not intercepted
unsupported for sparse patches"] M --> U N --> Y["Outside the supported sparse behavior"] X --> Y P -. "finally, after model.load_weights
returns or raises" .-> R["Restore the original Tensor.copy_"] ``` `CheckpointWeightPatch` represents either: - a dense checkpoint replacement (`indices=None`), or - a sparse checkpoint patch (`indices` and `values` over the full checkpoint shape). Sparse patches are expanded into checkpoint-shaped NaN staging tensors. The model's native loader maps those tensors into runtime-local destinations. For the supported single-copy loader path, the final same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_` keeps the existing destination at NaN positions and copies the changed values elsewhere. Patches are validated before the first load. Loader calls are bounded by a checkpoint-byte batching target, and a repeated checkpoint name begins a new loader call so repeated patches preserve input order. ### Scope and failure semantics The current implementation is intentionally narrow: - sparse patches require a floating checkpoint dtype and cannot carry NaN as a real update value; - the loader must preserve NaNs through checkpoint-to-runtime mapping and end in a same-shaped floating-point `Tensor.copy_`; - the validated integration uses exclusive, serialized weight updates and a single-copy loader; - composed/multi-stage loaders and custom write paths are not supported; - sparse application is not O(nnz): it allocates a full checkpoint-shaped NaN tensor and runs a dense `torch.where`/copy at the runtime destination; - updates are not transactional. A loader error can leave a partial update, so the caller must restore a known baseline or restart and reseed before serving. ### Companion VERL integration [VERL #7227](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7227) uses this API to add a vLLM consumer for VERL's `delta_sharded` checkpoint-engine wire format. The first update is a dense seed; steady updates contain checkpoint-coordinate indices and changed values. ### Duplication check I searched open vLLM PRs for checkpoint-coordinate weight patch loading and found no matching implementation. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/model_executor/model_loader \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py -q .venv/bin/ruff check --no-cache \ vllm/model_executor/model_loader/checkpoint_weight_patch.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check --no-cache \ vllm/model_executor/model_loader/checkpoint_weight_patch.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_checkpoint_weight_patch.py ``` The focused CPU test covers the dense seed, checkpoint-global sparse indices, TP-local slicing, packed Q/K destinations, repeated patch ordering, and restoration of `Tensor.copy_` after the supported path. The companion VERL integration tests additionally cover: - Qwen3-30B-A3B TP8+EP8 sparse-vs-dense and restore comparisons; - real CUDA IPC/ZMQ transfer through the companion VERL adapter; - a two-node full-NCCL versus `delta_sharded` weight-sync comparison. ## Test Result ### Focused repository test - Pytest: **1 passed**. - Ruff check: **passed**. - Ruff format check: **passed**. ### TP8+EP8 integration correctness Qwen3-30B-A3B, BF16, vLLM TP8+EP8: - 8/8 workers passed. - 32/32 selected runtime tensors matched the dense-load target with `torch.equal` after sparse apply. - 32/32 tensors returned to the checkpoint baseline after restore. - The probe covered packed QKV, norm, routed-expert `w13`, and routed-expert `w2` mappings. This is a representative runtime-tensor mapping probe, not a full-model digest or a phase-for-phase training-trajectory comparison. ### Companion VERL integration performance These are end-to-end results from the companion VERL integration, not a microbenchmark of this helper alone. | mode | steady samples | mean | median | range | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Full NCCL | 11 | 51.814 s | 51.812 s | 51.457-52.051 s | | `delta_sharded` + vLLM | 11 | 7.200 s | 7.740 s | 5.943-8.686 s | The ratio of means is **7.196x**; the conservative observed steady ratio is **5.924x**. The mean changed ratio was **0.646%**, and the mean sparse payload was **1129.4 MiB**. The one-time dense seed took **51.9 s** and is excluded from steady-state statistics. Environment: two nodes with 8 H20 GPUs per node; Qwen3-30B-A3B; FSDP1 trainer on one node; vLLM TP8+EP8 Triton-MoE rollout on the other; BF16; VERL V1 `separate_async`; NCCL `NET/Socket` over `eth0`; 12 delta and 12 full steps, with steps 2-12 used for the primary statistics. The two async jobs did not produce phase-aligned reward trajectories. The performance claim is limited to sustained weight-sync time; correctness comes from the independent bit-exact probe. ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex was used for code exploration, implementation assistance, testing, and review.

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Mamba prefix caching currently splits a prefill at the last block boundary

Let's use a 8k input as an example

Before

```bash
Model forward (7680 tokens) ->
FlashKDA(7680 tokens) ->
save checkpoint ->
Model forward (320 tokens) ->
FlashKDA(320 tokens)
```

Now

```bash
Model forward (8000 tokens) ->
FlashKDA(7680) ->
save checkpoint ->
FlashKDA(320)
```

This PR helps us avoid a second full-model pass through attention, MoE, routing, and TP collectives.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Ship rocprofiler-sdk 1.3.2 in Dockerfile.rocm_base to fix torch.profiler traces
commits.pr_body:
# [ROCm] Ship rocprofiler-sdk 1.3.2 in Dockerfile.rocm_base to fix torch.profiler HIP-graph traces

## Summary
The ROCm ≤ 7.2.3 base image (`rocm/dev-ubuntu-22.04:7.2.3-complete`) ships **rocprofiler-sdk 1.1.0**.
Since torch 2.12, PyTorch's Kineto GPU backend links `librocprofiler-sdk` (previously roctracer).
Under `torch.profiler`, rocprofiler-sdk **1.1.0** blows up `hipGraphLaunch` and disables the HIP
graph fast path, so profiled decode collapses GPU occupancy and profiled latency balloons —
making vLLM profiles unusable/misleading on gfx942/gfx950.

This is a **rocprofiler-sdk bug fixed in 1.3.2**. This PR builds rocprofiler-sdk 1.3.2
(`ROCm/rocm-systems @ 2b22ab0`) in a dedicated stage and overlays it onto `/opt/rocm` in the
final base image. torch/Kineto links `librocprofiler-sdk.so.1` by soname, so swapping the
runtime lib is sufficient — **no torch rebuild**, `build_pytorch` is untouched.

Self-removing: drop the stage + COPY once `BASE_IMAGE` ships rocprofiler-sdk ≥ 1.3.2 (ROCm 7.14,
tracked in #48826).

## Not a duplicate
Checked open PRs/issues (`rocprofiler`, `rocprofiler-sdk`, `kineto`, `roctracer`): no PR changes
the base image's rocprofiler-sdk. Related: #48826 (ROCm 7.14 migration — the eventual superseder)
and closed/stale #39162 (same `rocprofiler_configure in libtorch_cpu.so` observation, no fix).

## Evidence (gfx942 / MI300X, torch 2.12, llama-3.1-8B, `bench latency --profile`)
Measured on an image produced by this exact change (`docker build` of the new stage +
`COPY`/`ldconfig`, then the vLLM layer):
| rocprofiler-sdk | GPU occupancy | gaps >1ms | hipGraphLaunch avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1.0 (base) | 39.9% | 578 | 16.6 ms |
| **1.3.2 (this PR)** | **97.8%** | **2** | **893 µs** |

Microbench (HIP graph replay under profiler): `hipGraphLaunch` 380 µs → 56 µs (≈ roctracer's
50 µs). ROCm 7.14 (native rocprofiler-sdk 1.3.2) independently shows the healthy result (98.6%
occupancy at e2e), confirming the rocprofiler-sdk version is the fix.

## Test commands
```
# Base image build (surgical stage builds in-context; rest of the base is unchanged):
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base -t <base>:rocprofsdk-1.3.2 .
docker run --rm <base>:rocprofsdk-1.3.2 bash -c \
  'ldd $(python -c "import torch,pathlib;print(pathlib.Path(torch.__file__).parent/\"lib\")")/libtorch_cpu.so | grep rocprofiler-sdk; \
   cat /app/versions.txt | grep ROCPROFILER_SDK'
# expect: librocprofiler-sdk.so.1 -> ...1.3.2

# llama profile (on a vLLM image built from this base):
VLLM_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=/tmp/prof vllm bench latency --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  -tp 1 --batch-size 32 --input-len 512 --output-len 128 --num-iters 3 \
  --profile --profiler-config.profiler=torch --profiler-config.torch_profiler_dir=/tmp/prof
# expect: profiled GPU occupancy ~99%, hipGraphLaunch sub-ms (vs ~16ms on 1.1.0)
```

## Notes
- Adds a ~few-minute rocprofiler-sdk compile to base-image builds (uses `sccache` when
  `USE_SCCACHE=1`, matching the existing stages).
- Pinned commit is overridable via `--build-arg ROCPROFILER_SDK_COMMIT=...`.

## AI assistance
Developed with AI assistance (Claude): the investigation, the Dockerfile stage, and the
build + llama-profile validation above were AI-run on the submitter's MI300X box. Opened as
a **draft** pending the submitter's final line-by-line review before marking ready.
